walkthroughs.body_html:
A startup is a brand-new business in its first months.

Every startup needs:

  • A clear idea.
  • Some money to begin.
  • A plan showing how it will work.
  • People — even if it's only you. 🤝

Money put into a business is called capital. It might come from:

  • Your own savings.
  • Family and friends.
  • A bank loan — borrowed cash you must repay with interest.
  • An investor who buys a share of the business.

No money, no startup. 💷

Your brand is the name, logo, and feel of your business.

Strong brands like Nike or Lego are easy to spot and easy to trust.

A startup picks a clear name, a simple logo, and a story that customers remember. 🏷️

mcqs.q: Which sector does manufacturing belong to?
options: The secondary sector — which transforms raw materials from the primary sector (farming, mining) into finished goods.
Manufacturing is in the primary sector because it makes things.
Manufacturing is in the tertiary sector along with services.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.

mcqs.q: How does HRM differ from traditional personnel management?
options: HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
HRM and personnel are exactly the same thing — just a name change.
Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.
HRM treats people as a strategic asset and integrates human resource policies with business strategy; personnel management is more administrative and reactive, handling hiring, pay and disputes.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary market research?
options: Primary research is done first and secondary research is done later.
Primary research is the most important and secondary research is less important.
Primary research is original data the business gathers itself (surveys, interviews); secondary research uses existing data (reports, government statistics, market intelligence).
HRM only applies to large multinational companies.
